decisions.executionNote: Raise the left arm in elbow-up configuration and begin orienting toward the leftmost tube; right arm stays home.
Use smaller continuous increments after the guard; advance above the leftmost tube while pitching the open gripper down.
Align the left gripper with the tube axis and approach from above; keeping clearance before closing.
Fine-align from the wrist image: shift toward the cap and center the tube between the fingers, then settle at grasp height.
Close on the centered first tube, then lift gently to check retention from the wrist view.
The first tube is visibly retained. Lift clear and start rotating it upright while moving toward the rack's left slot.
Continue the held tube's upright rotation and position above the left side of the rack, maintaining overhead clearance.
Lower the nearly upright first tube toward the left front large hole, making a small lateral alignment correction.
Insert vertically another four centimeters into the aligned leftmost large slot, keeping the tube closed in the gripper.
The tube appears supported upright in the slot. Open and withdraw without pulling it, then inspect its seating.
The released tube toppled rather than seating. Clear the rack and approach the remaining left tube while the displaced tube settles; insertion alignment needs correction.
Advance above the second left tube and finish the downward grasp orientation with a slow, continuous elbow-up approach.
Lower onto the centered second tube and close on its body, using its wrist silhouette for alignment.
Lift the second tube clear, then start its upright rotation. Use a more rearward-aligned slot approach than the first attempt.
Rotate the retained tube toward upright and bring it over a central-left large slot, keeping the tip above the rack.
Finish upright orientation above the rack before descending; keep the tube retained and maintain arm configuration continuity.
Correct the tube toward the front row's second large hole using the head projection, then descend cautiously toward engagement.
Continue a slow vertical insertion while monitoring whether the tube stays fixed relative to the fingers or meets the rack surface.
The tube shifted in the fingers at the rim. Lift slightly and correct five millimeters left and eight toward the robot before trying the slot again.
Ease down another fourteen millimeters at the corrected slot center, then open in place to let the tube settle without dragging it.
The tip appears to be resting on the rack surface rather than seated. Regrasp, lift, and shift toward the adjacent central large opening for a clearer alignment.
Make a small wrist-image lateral correction over the visible opening and reduce the tube's lean before easing down.
The tube tip is now centered over the visible central opening. Lower three centimeters slowly while retaining it.
Seat the tube a final few millimeters, open in place, then back away gently to verify that it remains upright in the slot.
Withdraw the open left gripper well clear of the rack and inspect whether the released tube settles into its opening.
The released tube remains in the rack. Clear the left arm and begin an elbow-up approach to the right-side tube with the right gripper.
Advance the right arm over its tube while rotating to match the cap direction. Retract the left arm toward home, remaining in separate workspaces.
Finish the right tube's top-down approach and return the empty left arm home.
Use the right wrist silhouette to center and match the tube's tilt, lower to grasp height, and close.
Keep the right gripper closed and lift the tube clear to verify retention before transporting it.
Transport the visibly retained right tube toward the rack and rotate it toward upright while maintaining tip clearance.
Finish the upright rotation and position the right-held tube above the rack's rightmost large slot; inspect before insertion.
Center the right tube over the rightmost front opening and lower toward the rack while retaining it.
Continue the right tube's vertical insertion slowly, checking for any slip against the rack rim.
The right tube met the rim. Lift slightly, correct six millimeters outward toward the large hole center, and retry a gentle descent.
Retry with a small rearward correction and slightly inward centering, lifting before the lateral motion to avoid dragging the tip.
Ease the right tube down a final short distance, open in place, and withdraw enough to inspect the actual seating rather than relying on tracking.
The right tube has dropped into its opening. Withdraw the right gripper, and raise the left arm to inspect and straighten the leaning central tube.
Approach the leaning center tube from the front-left to regrasp it while the empty right arm retracts toward home.
Replan with smaller increments after the continuity guard, bringing the left gripper toward the leaning tube without crossing arms.
Bring the left fingers near the upper part of the leaning tube for a corrective grasp; finish returning the right arm to its home region.
Move the open left fingers around the leaning tube's upper body using the wrist view; keep the upright right tube untouched.
Close around the leaning tube's body and lift it clear of the rack before correcting its tilt.
The tube is retained after regrasp. Correct its forward lean while lifting the wrist to keep its grasp point clear of the rack.
The corrected tube now appears parallel to the upright right tube. Move its tip rearward over the central opening, then lower gently.
The tip is still forward of the central large aperture. Lift slightly and shift rearward toward that opening before a short descent.
Center the visible tube tip a few millimeters over the large hole, then release it vertically to settle without driving the fingers into the rack.
Clear the open fingers from the tube and allow it to settle freely into the centered aperture, then inspect upright seating.
The central tube was displaced out of the rack. Clear the left fingers and let it settle behind the rack before planning recovery; leave the seated right tube untouched.
Approach the displaced tube from the rack's left side at clearance height, keeping the elbow-up configuration and checking reach.
Advance above the rack toward the displaced tube, retaining clearance and monitoring the arm's reach and elbow continuity.
After the reach guard, use a shallower front approach to the displaced tube instead of extending farther with the wrist pitched down.
